findings.title: Restart loop: telemetryd crashed 4 times
findings.detail: telemetryd crashed 4 times in this log window. A supervisor such as the High Availability Manager (HAM) is restarting it, but the root cause is unfixed -- the system is running without this service for part of every cycle.
findings.action: Treat the *first* crash of the process as the real bug and fix that crash; do not just tune the supervisor's restart policy -- that only hides the fault.

findings.title: Event burst at 08:06
findings.detail: 25 events in one minute vs an average of 8.5/min (3 of them errors). Bursts like this usually mark the moment a failure cascaded -- start the investigation at this timestamp.

findings.title: Message sent to a process that no longer exists (ESRCH) (x6)
findings.detail: In QNX native message passing, MsgSend() returned ESRCH: the destination process (or its channel) was gone when the client tried to send. Typically the server crashed or restarted and the client kept a stale connection id (coid).
findings.action: Check whether the destination process crashed just before these errors (look for a crash cluster at the same timestamp). Clients should re-attach (name_open/ConnectAttach) when a server restarts instead of caching the coid forever.

findings.title: Storage (CAM/devb) error (x2)
findings.detail: The block driver stack (devb-* / CAM) reported a storage error: command timeouts, resets or media errors. Repeated errors point at failing media or a cabling/power problem rather than software.
findings.action: Check the same device for escalating error counts, run the drive's SMART/health check, and plan media replacement if errors cluster on one device.
